note: V92Parameters is 54 constant stores and three tiny members, so the set is small on purpose: there is no arithmetic to break.  What it has to show is that the constant table is CHECKED rather than merely present on both sides -- one value moved, one float moved in its last digit, one store removed -- and that the three members really run.

label: one integer default moves by one
the negative default loses its sign
one float default moves in its last digit
the largest float default is out by a factor of ten
the first field of the object is not written
the last field of the object is not written
the constructor does not call init
the constructor does not store its argument
the destructor is not empty
why: Same as v90params.json's entry of the same name, and for the same reason: GCC's `-flifetime-dse` is on at -O2 and deletes stores to `*this` in a destructor, so the mutated body and the empty one compile to the identical bare `ret`.  No mutation confined to the destroyed object can be caught here.
